rows.section: Personal income tax (φόρος εισοδήματος) from tax year 2026
rows.basis: Annual taxable income (calendar tax year), after exemptions and deductions
rows.note: The 2026 tax reform (Law 244(I)/2025) raised the tax-free amount from €19,500 to €22,000 and widened the bands; the top rate of 35% now starts above €72,000. Employers withhold the tax monthly (PAYE) using the deductions the employee declares on form T.D.59. Self-employed profits are taxed on the same scale.
rows.source_title: Tax Department: Declaration for claiming tax deductions for the tax year 2026 (Form T.D.59A, English), Part C Tax computation

rows.section: Personal deductions from 2026 (new article 14B and other deductions)
rows.label: Dependent child deduction: first child
rows.basis: Deducted from taxable income, euro per tax year
rows.note: Only Cyprus tax residents get the new deductions; they are subject to the income limits below (except home insurance) and are not transferable between spouses. A dependent child is under 18, a secondary school pupil under 20, in the National Guard under 21, a full-time student up to 24, or permanently unable to support themselves (status at 31 December).

rows.section: Special defence contribution (έκτακτη εισφορά για την άμυνα) on investment income
rows.label: Dividends paid out of profits from 2026 onwards
rows.basis: Gross dividends and interest, withheld at source or self-assessed
rows.note: The Special Defence Contribution (Amending) (No. 4) Law 2025 cut the rate on dividends from 17% to 5% and ended the deemed dividend distribution for profits from 2026. GHS at 2.65% is also due on dividends and interest.

rows.section: Employee contributions
rows.label: Social insurance (Social Insurance Fund)
rows.basis: Gross earnings; social insurance up to €5,742 a month (€1,325 a week), GHS on income up to €180,000 a year
rows.note: The employer deducts the employee's share from pay. Where an occupational pension scheme is run without employee contributions, the employee pays 4.45% and the employer 13.15% social insurance. The state adds 5.2% to the Social Insurance Fund. Both contributions are deductible from taxable income.
rows.source_title: Social Insurance Services (Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance): Employer's Guide (PDF), section Amount of contributions
